$comment: Rule catalog — data. Standards 3, 4, 17. Provenance, versioning, and lineage: the three records that make it possible to say what a model was trained on and whether a feature could legitimately have been used. Two entries carry detectors, and both detect the absence of a document rather than the truth of one.

rules.title: Dataset provenance is recorded and discoverable
rules.description: Every dataset has a written record of where it came from, when it was obtained, what population or process it represents, what each row is, and what was excluded from it — discoverable from the dataset rather than only from the memory of whoever built it.
rules.rationale: A dataset is a claim about the world, and the claim cannot be assessed without knowing how it was obtained and what was left out. Exclusions matter most and are recorded least: dropping rows with missing values does not remove noise, it removes the population for whom that field is missing.
rules.remediation: Add a dataset card — DATASET.md or DATA_CARD.md — covering origin, collection mechanism, population, unit of observation, and an exclusions section listing each rule applied with the count and proportion it removed.
rules.evidenceExpected: A provenance document carrying origin, collection, population, and exclusions sections, plus an attestation that the exclusions listed are all of them.
rules.$assuranceNote: The check establishes that a provenance document exists and carries the expected sections. It cannot establish that the content is accurate, current, or complete, and it can never detect an exclusion that was applied and not written down — the evidence of the removal is precisely what was removed.

rules.title: Observations are not removed to improve a metric
rules.description: Observations must not be removed because of what their removal does to a reported number. The prohibited act is the combination: removal, driven by the metric, undisclosed.
rules.rationale: Removing hard cases raises every score while removing exactly the population the model most needs to handle. The resulting figure describes performance on a problem nobody has.
rules.remediation: Restore the excluded observations and re-evaluate, or justify the exclusion by a rule that was specified before the results were seen and record it with its effect.
rules.evidenceExpected: An attestation that each exclusion was rule-driven and pre-specified rather than selected after a disappointing evaluation, with the provenance document's exclusions section as supporting evidence.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. An exclusion applied before results were seen and one applied after them are byte-identical in the code that performs them; the difference is intent and sequence, neither of which is in the repository.

rules.title: Datasets carry an identifier that changes with their contents
rules.description: Each dataset carries an identifier — a version, a content hash, a manifest of files and checksums, or a data-versioning tool's revision — that differs whenever the contents differ. A filename is not an identifier.
rules.rationale: A dataset that can change while its name stays the same makes every past result unverifiable and every comparison unsound: two models said to have been evaluated on the same data may not have been, and nothing records which.
rules.remediation: Add a versioning mechanism beside the data — a .dvc file, a lockfile, a manifest, or adjacent checksums — and cite the identifier from the experiment records that used it.
rules.evidenceExpected: A version manifest, lockfile, or checksum set covering the datasets in use, and experiment records naming the version each result came from.
rules.$assuranceNote: The check establishes that data exists and that no pinning mechanism was found beside it. Its silence establishes only that a mechanism exists — not that the identifier changes when the contents do, not that the training run used the version the manifest names, and not that any result cited it.

rules.title: Each feature's sources, transformation, and availability time are recorded
rules.description: For every feature, a record names the raw sources it derives from, the transformation that produced it, and when its underlying data becomes available relative to the prediction moment.
rules.rationale: Lineage exists to make two other reviews possible: whether a feature will exist at inference, and whether it encodes the target. Both are properties of where a value comes from and when — never of the value itself — so without the record, neither question can be answered reliably.
rules.remediation: Build a feature register, documented schema, or feature-store definition naming sources, transformations, and availability timing per feature, and keep it current with the transformation code.
rules.evidenceExpected: A lineage record sufficient to answer, for each feature, whether it derives from information unavailable at prediction time and whether it derives from the target.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. A scanner can see that a function consumes one column and produces another; it cannot see that the source column is populated by a nightly job that runs after the event being predicted. A name-and-dtype listing and a genuine lineage record are indistinguishable to a scan.
